quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane on a two-lane road. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. What should you do if a driver behind you wants to go faster?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass, go fast, or turn left. Use the right lane when you are going slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use the parking brake and put the car in park.
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake and put the car in park.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake and leave the car in park when parked on a hill. If there is a curb, point your front wheels toward it when going uphill or away from it when going downhill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels so the car rolls away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You want to pass a motorcycle. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small.
Honk to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.
Stay completely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay completely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle its own full lane when passing. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to your lane too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles pulling trailers may not see you behind them. Increase your distance from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road, so more distance helps you see ahead.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are going the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green to proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
There is construction or road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is construction or road work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs warn of construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. These signs help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Fines for traffic violations may double in these areas.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes and shift to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake. Steer in the direction you want the front to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: A car cuts in front of you suddenly. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Honk and press the brake firmly.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space without requiring you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue to the next exit and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the freeway. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect a car backing up and will likely crash into you.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and less reliable.

questions.question: In rainy weather, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. During this time, oil from cars mixes with rainwater on the pavement, making it very slippery.

questions.question: If you are continually being passed on the right and the left while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the lane on your right.
Move to the lane on your left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane on your right.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On an interstate highway, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: If you are being passed in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to the drive lane safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead on the road.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light and are moving in your direction.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road construction/maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction/maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stalled out of sight. Slow down so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the road safely.

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left side of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: To turn left from a two-way street, start in the lane closest to the centerline. Begin your turn as your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
They brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a regular vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the motorcyclist at risk. You need enough time and distance to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist makes a mistake.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before the turn.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, unless a sign says you cannot. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You may move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on the road?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for the work zone.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the work zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop for equipment in the work zone. Driving carefully protects drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: The first 30 minutes of rainfall is most dangerous. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet, making the road very slippery. Drive with extra caution on wet roads.

questions.question: If you cannot find a gap in traffic to enter the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap in traffic. Do not drive to the end of the ramp and stop. You will not have enough space to speed up to match traffic before entering the freeway.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and your head against the head restraint. Grip the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: When exiting an alley or driveway onto a sidewalk, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.
